LECTURE 11 Stage 2: Tokenization & Data

Positional Embeddings

Teaching the model where each word sits in the sequence
⏱ 45 min read 💻 Hands-on coding 🎯 Intermediate

Why Does Position Matter?

Consider these two sentences:

  • "Dog bites man" — a mundane event
  • "Man bites dog" — headline news!

Same words, completely different meanings. The order of words is essential to understanding language. But here is the problem: our token embeddings from Lecture 10 assign the exact same vector to "dog" regardless of whether it appears first or last in a sentence. The embedding layer has no concept of position.

This is fundamentally different from recurrent neural networks (RNNs), which process tokens one at a time in order. Transformers, by contrast, process all tokens simultaneously in parallel. This parallelism is what makes them fast, but it means they have no inherent notion of sequence order. We must explicitly inject position information.

💡 Analogy: Seat Numbers in a Theater

Think of tokens as audience members and the sequence as a theater. The word "love" means the same thing no matter who says it (token embedding), but the model needs to know it is sitting in seat 3, not seat 7 — because where it sits changes the meaning of the sentence. Positional embeddings are like seat number tags that each token wears.

The Problem: Transformers Are Position-Blind

To make this concrete, consider how a Transformer processes a sequence. After the token embedding layer, we have a matrix of shape (sequence_length, embed_dim). Without positional information, the model sees this as a set (unordered collection), not a sequence (ordered list).

The Position Problem

"The cat sat"                    "sat cat The"

Token embeddings:                Token embeddings:
┌──────────┐                     ┌──────────┐
│ emb("The") │                     │ emb("sat") │
│ emb("cat") │   No position      │ emb("cat") │   No position
│ emb("sat") │  ============>     │ emb("The") │  ============>
└──────────┘    Same bag of       └──────────┘    Same bag of
                 vectors!                          vectors!

  Without position info, these are IDENTICAL to the model.

We need a way to make each position unique. The two main approaches are sinusoidal encoding and learned embeddings.

Approach 1: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding

The original "Attention Is All You Need" paper (Vaswani et al., 2017) proposed using sine and cosine functions of different frequencies to encode position. The formula is:

# For even dimensions (2i):
PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

# For odd dimensions (2i+1):
PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

This creates a unique pattern for each position. The key properties:

🔍 Unique Patterns

Each position gets a distinct vector. No two positions share the same encoding.

📏 Bounded Values

Sine and cosine are always between -1 and +1, keeping values numerically stable.

♻️ Relative Positions

The model can learn to attend to relative positions because PE(pos+k) can be expressed as a linear function of PE(pos).

🔄 Generalization

Can extrapolate to sequence lengths not seen during training (in theory).

Python
import numpy as np

def sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model):
    """
    Create sinusoidal positional encodings.

    Args:
        max_len: Maximum sequence length
        d_model: Embedding dimension (must be even)
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (max_len, d_model)
    """
    pe = np.zeros((max_len, d_model))
    position = np.arange(max_len).reshape(-1, 1)  # (max_len, 1)

    # Compute the division term: 10000^(2i/d_model)
    div_term = np.exp(
        np.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )

    # Apply sin to even indices, cos to odd indices
    pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(position * div_term)  # even dims
    pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(position * div_term)  # odd dims

    return pe

# Generate encodings
max_len = 20
d_model = 16
pe = sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model)

print(f"Positional encoding shape: {pe.shape}")
print(f"  (max_len={max_len}, d_model={d_model})")

# Show encodings for first few positions
print(f"\\nPosition 0: {pe[0, :8].round(3)}...")
print(f"Position 1: {pe[1, :8].round(3)}...")
print(f"Position 2: {pe[2, :8].round(3)}...")

# Show that each position is unique
print(f"\\n=== Position Uniqueness ===")
for i in range(5):
    for j in range(i+1, 5):
        sim = np.dot(pe[i], pe[j]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[i]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[j]))
        print(f"  Similarity(pos_{i}, pos_{j}) = {sim:.4f}")

# Nearby positions are more similar than distant ones
print(f"\\n=== Distance Patterns ===")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_1)  = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[1]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[1])):.4f} (adjacent)")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_10) = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[10]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[10])):.4f} (distant)")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_19) = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[19]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[19])):.4f} (very distant)")

Visualizing Position Patterns

The sinusoidal encoding creates a distinctive wave pattern. Lower dimensions oscillate slowly (capturing broad positional information), while higher dimensions oscillate rapidly (capturing fine-grained position).

Python
import numpy as np

def sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model):
    pe = np.zeros((max_len, d_model))
    position = np.arange(max_len).reshape(-1, 1)
    div_term = np.exp(np.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model))
    pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(position * div_term)
    pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(position * div_term)
    return pe

max_len = 50
d_model = 32
pe = sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model)

# Visualize as a text-based heatmap
print("=== Positional Encoding Heatmap (first 20 positions, 16 dims) ===")
print("      " + "".join(f" d{i:<3}" for i in range(0, 16)))
print("      " + "-" * 64)

for pos in range(20):
    row = f"p{pos:<3} | "
    for dim in range(16):
        val = pe[pos, dim]
        if val > 0.5:
            row += "  ++ "
        elif val > 0.0:
            row += "  +  "
        elif val > -0.5:
            row += "  -  "
        else:
            row += "  -- "
    print(row)

print("\\nLegend: ++ (>0.5), + (0 to 0.5), - (-0.5 to 0), -- (<-0.5)")
print("\\nNotice: Low dimensions (d0,d1) change slowly across positions")
print("        High dimensions (d14,d15) oscillate more rapidly")

# Show the wave pattern for specific dimensions
print("\\n=== Dimension 0 (slow wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 0] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")

print("=== Dimension 6 (medium wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 6] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")

print("=== Dimension 14 (fast wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 14] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")
print("(* = positive, . = negative)")

Approach 2: Learned Positional Embeddings (GPT-2)

GPT-2 takes a simpler approach: instead of computing positions with formulas, it learns a separate embedding for each position, just like it learns token embeddings. This is simply another embedding lookup table, but indexed by position rather than token ID.

Property Sinusoidal (Original Transformer) Learned (GPT-2)
How it works Fixed mathematical formula Learned during training
Trainable? No (fixed) Yes (backpropagation)
Extrapolation Can extend beyond training length Limited to max training length
Parameters Zero additional parameters max_len × d_model parameters
Performance Good Slightly better in practice
Used by Original Transformer, some models GPT-2, GPT-3, BERT
Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    """Simple embedding layer."""
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

# === GPT-2 Style: Learned Positional Embeddings ===
np.random.seed(42)

vocab_size = 100
max_seq_len = 20
embed_dim = 8

# TWO separate embedding tables
token_embedding = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)  # shape: (100, 8)
position_embedding = Embedding(max_seq_len, embed_dim)  # shape: (20, 8)

print(f"Token embedding table:    ({vocab_size}, {embed_dim})")
print(f"Position embedding table: ({max_seq_len}, {embed_dim})")
print(f"Total embedding parameters: {vocab_size * embed_dim + max_seq_len * embed_dim:,}")

# Simulate processing a sentence
token_ids = [42, 17, 88, 3, 56]  # 5 tokens
seq_len = len(token_ids)

# Token embeddings: look up by token ID
tok_emb = token_embedding.forward(token_ids)
print(f"\\nToken embeddings shape: {tok_emb.shape}")

# Position embeddings: look up by position index [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
position_ids = list(range(seq_len))
pos_emb = position_embedding.forward(position_ids)
print(f"Position embeddings shape: {pos_emb.shape}")

# === THE KEY STEP: Add them together! ===
input_embeddings = tok_emb + pos_emb
print(f"Combined embeddings shape: {input_embeddings.shape}")

# Show the combination for one token
print(f"\\n=== Token at position 0 (token_id=42) ===")
print(f"  Token embedding:    {tok_emb[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position embedding: {pos_emb[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Combined (sum):     {input_embeddings[0].round(3)}")

# The same token at different positions gets different representations!
print(f"\\n=== Same token (id=42) at different positions ===")
same_tok = token_embedding.forward([42, 42, 42])
diff_pos = position_embedding.forward([0, 5, 15])
combined = same_tok + diff_pos
print(f"  Position  0: {combined[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position  5: {combined[1].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position 15: {combined[2].round(3)}")
print("  Same word, different representations due to position!")

# GPT-2 scale
print(f"\\n--- GPT-2 Scale ---")
print(f"Position embedding table: ({1024}, {768})")
print(f"Position parameters: {1024 * 768:,} = ~786K")
print(f"Max sequence length: 1024 tokens")
✅ Why Addition, Not Concatenation?

You might wonder: why do we add token and position embeddings instead of concatenating them? Addition keeps the dimensionality the same (d_model), while concatenation would double it to 2 * d_model. Research shows that addition works just as well, and the model learns to use different dimensions for token vs. position information during training. This also keeps the architecture simpler and more memory-efficient.

The Complete Input Representation

Let us now see the full picture of how GPT-2 constructs its input:

GPT-2 Input Pipeline

Raw text: "The cat sat on the mat"
              |
              v
      ┌───────────────┐
      │   Tokenizer   │
      └───────────────┘
              |
              v
Token IDs: [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]
              |                        |
              v                        v
   ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
   │ Token Embedding  │    │ Position Embedding│
   │ table (50257x768)│    │ table (1024x768) │
   └──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘
              |                        |
              v                        v
   tok_emb (6, 768)        pos_emb (6, 768)
              \\                       /
               \\                     /
                \\      Element-     /
                 \\   wise ADD     /
                  v              v
            ┌──────────────────────┐
            │  input_emb (6, 768)  │
            │  = tok_emb + pos_emb │
            └──────────────────────┘
                      |
                      v
              To Transformer Layers
Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale
    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

class GPT2InputEmbedding:
    """
    Complete GPT-2 input embedding: token + position.
    This is what the first layer of GPT-2 does.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, max_seq_len, embed_dim):
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len
        self.token_embedding = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.position_embedding = Embedding(max_seq_len, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, token_ids):
        seq_len = len(token_ids)
        if seq_len > self.max_seq_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds maximum {self.max_seq_len}"
            )

        # Token embeddings
        tok_emb = self.token_embedding.forward(token_ids)

        # Position embeddings (positions 0, 1, 2, ..., seq_len-1)
        pos_ids = list(range(seq_len))
        pos_emb = self.position_embedding.forward(pos_ids)

        # Combine by addition
        return tok_emb + pos_emb

# === Full pipeline demo ===
np.random.seed(42)

model_input = GPT2InputEmbedding(
    vocab_size=50257,   # GPT-2 vocabulary
    max_seq_len=1024,   # GPT-2 max context
    embed_dim=768       # GPT-2 embedding dimension
)

# Simulated token IDs (as if from a BPE tokenizer)
token_ids = [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]
words = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]

print("=== GPT-2 Input Embedding Pipeline ===")
print(f"Input tokens: {list(zip(words, token_ids))}")

input_emb = model_input.forward(token_ids)
print(f"Output shape: {input_emb.shape}")
print(f"  ({len(token_ids)} tokens, each with 768-dim embedding)")

# Show that "the" (pos 0) and "the" (pos 4) now differ
print(f"\\n'The' at position 0: [{input_emb[0][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"'the' at position 4: [{input_emb[4][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"Same word, different positions -> different representations!")

# Total parameters
tok_params = 50257 * 768
pos_params = 1024 * 768
print(f"\\n--- Parameter Count ---")
print(f"Token embedding:    {tok_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Position embedding: {pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Total input layer:  {tok_params + pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"That is {(tok_params + pos_params) / 1e6:.1f}M parameters just for the input!")

Max Sequence Length and Its Implications

With learned positional embeddings, the model has a hard maximum sequence length. GPT-2 was trained with max_seq_len = 1024, meaning it can only process sequences up to 1024 tokens. If you try to feed it more, the model simply does not have position embeddings for positions beyond 1023.

This is one of the key limitations that newer approaches try to address:

📏 RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding)

Used in LLaMA and many modern models. Encodes position as rotations in 2D subspaces, enabling better extrapolation to longer sequences.

🔗 ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases)

Used in BLOOM. Adds a linear bias based on token distance directly in the attention scores, with no position embeddings needed.

📚 Connection to the Book

In "Build an LLM from Scratch," Raschka implements the GPT-2 approach with learned positional embeddings. The cfg["context_length"] parameter (1024 for GPT-2) determines the size of the position embedding table. This is defined right at the start of the model class, alongside the token embedding layer.

Relative vs. Absolute Positional Encodings

Everything we have discussed so far uses absolute positions: position 0, position 1, etc. An alternative is relative positional encoding, which encodes the distance between tokens rather than their absolute positions.

Aspect Absolute (GPT-2) Relative (T5, etc.)
What is encoded Position index (0, 1, 2, ...) Distance between tokens (i - j)
Where applied Added to input embeddings Added to attention scores
Length generalization Limited to training length Better generalization
Complexity Simple lookup table More complex implementation

For our GPT-2 implementation, we will stick with absolute learned embeddings — they are simpler and work well in practice.

⚠️ Common Mistake

A common error when implementing positional embeddings is forgetting to limit the sequence length. If your model's position embedding table has 1024 entries and you feed it a sequence of 1025 tokens, you will get an index-out-of-bounds error. Always validate input length against max_seq_len before processing.

Summary

📌 Key Takeaways

  • Transformers process all tokens in parallel and have no inherent sense of order
  • Positional embeddings encode where each token sits in the sequence
  • GPT-2 uses learned positional embeddings (a second lookup table)
  • Token + position embeddings are added element-wise to form the input
  • Max sequence length is fixed by the position embedding table size

👉 What is Next

We now have the complete input representation for our LLM. In Lecture 12, we will build the full data preprocessing pipeline that takes raw text and outputs training-ready batches of embedded token sequences.

🧠 Quick Check

Q1: Why do Transformers need positional embeddings but RNNs do not?

A: RNNs process tokens one at a time in sequence, so position is implicit in the processing order. Transformers process all tokens in parallel, so position must be explicitly encoded.

Q2: What is the shape of GPT-2's position embedding table?

A: (1024, 768) — 1024 positions (max sequence length) times 768 embedding dimensions, totaling ~786K parameters.

Q3: Why add token and position embeddings instead of concatenating them?

A: Addition preserves the embedding dimension (d_model), keeping the architecture simpler and more memory-efficient. The model learns to partition dimensions for token vs. position information during training.

LECȚIA 11 Etapa 2: Tokenizare & Date

Embedding-uri poziționale

Învățând modelul unde se află fiecare cuvânt în secvență
⏱ 45 min lectură 💻 Exerciții practice de cod 🎯 Intermediar

De ce contează poziția?

Considerați aceste două propoziții:

  • „Dog bites man” — un eveniment banal
  • „Man bites dog” — știre de primă pagină!

Aceleași cuvinte, semnificații complet diferite. Ordinea cuvintelor este esențială pentru înțelegerea limbajului. Dar iată problema: embedding-urile noastre de token-uri din Lecția 10 atribuie exact același vector cuvântului „dog” indiferent dacă apare primul sau ultimul într-o propoziție. Stratul de embedding nu are niciun concept de poziție.

Acest lucru este fundamental diferit de rețelele neuronale recurente (RNN), care procesează token-urile unul câte unul, în ordine. Transformer-ele, prin contrast, procesează toate token-urile simultan, în paralel. Acest paralelism este ceea ce le face rapide, dar înseamnă că nu au o noțiune inerentă de ordine a secvenței. Trebuie să injectăm explicit informația de poziție.

💡 Analogie: Numerele locurilor într-un teatru

Gândiți-vă la token-uri ca la spectatori și la secvență ca la un teatru. Cuvântul „love” înseamnă același lucru indiferent cine îl spune (embedding-ul token-ului), dar modelul trebuie să știe că stă pe locul 3, nu pe locul 7 — pentru că locul pe care stă schimbă semnificația propoziției. Embedding-urile poziționale sunt ca niște ecusoane cu numărul locului pe care le poartă fiecare token.

Problema: Transformer-ele sunt oarbe la poziție

Pentru a face acest lucru concret, considerați modul în care un Transformer procesează o secvență. După stratul de embedding al token-urilor, avem o matrice de forma (sequence_length, embed_dim). Fără informație pozițională, modelul vede aceasta ca o mulțime (colecție neordonată), nu ca o secvență (listă ordonată).

Problema poziției

"The cat sat"                    "sat cat The"

Token embeddings:                Token embeddings:
┌──────────┐                     ┌──────────┐
│ emb("The") │                     │ emb("sat") │
│ emb("cat") │   Fără poziție     │ emb("cat") │   Fără poziție
│ emb("sat") │  ============>     │ emb("The") │  ============>
└──────────┘    Aceeași mulțime    └──────────┘    Aceeași mulțime
                 de vectori!                          de vectori!

  Fără informație de poziție, acestea sunt IDENTICE pentru model.

Avem nevoie de o modalitate de a face fiecare poziție unică. Cele două abordări principale sunt codificarea sinusoidală și embedding-urile învățate.

Abordarea 1: Codificarea pozițională sinusoidală

Lucrarea originală „Attention Is All You Need” (Vaswani et al., 2017) a propus utilizarea funcțiilor sinus și cosinus de frecvențe diferite pentru codificarea poziției. Formula este:

# For even dimensions (2i):
PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

# For odd dimensions (2i+1):
PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

Aceasta creează un model unic pentru fiecare poziție. Proprietățile cheie:

🔍 Modele unice

Fiecare poziție primește un vector distinct. Nu există două poziții care să împartă aceeași codificare.

📏 Valori limitate

Sinusul și cosinusul sunt întotdeauna între -1 și +1, menținând valorile numeric stabile.

♻️ Poziții relative

Modelul poate învăța să acorde atenție pozițiilor relative deoarece PE(pos+k) poate fi exprimat ca o funcție liniară a PE(pos).

🔄 Generalizare

Poate extrapola la lungimi de secvență nevăzute în timpul antrenamentului (în teorie).

Python
import numpy as np

def sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model):
    """
    Create sinusoidal positional encodings.

    Args:
        max_len: Maximum sequence length
        d_model: Embedding dimension (must be even)
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (max_len, d_model)
    """
    pe = np.zeros((max_len, d_model))
    position = np.arange(max_len).reshape(-1, 1)  # (max_len, 1)

    # Compute the division term: 10000^(2i/d_model)
    div_term = np.exp(
        np.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )

    # Apply sin to even indices, cos to odd indices
    pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(position * div_term)  # even dims
    pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(position * div_term)  # odd dims

    return pe

# Generate encodings
max_len = 20
d_model = 16
pe = sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model)

print(f"Positional encoding shape: {pe.shape}")
print(f"  (max_len={max_len}, d_model={d_model})")

# Show encodings for first few positions
print(f"\\nPosition 0: {pe[0, :8].round(3)}...")
print(f"Position 1: {pe[1, :8].round(3)}...")
print(f"Position 2: {pe[2, :8].round(3)}...")

# Show that each position is unique
print(f"\\n=== Position Uniqueness ===")
for i in range(5):
    for j in range(i+1, 5):
        sim = np.dot(pe[i], pe[j]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[i]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[j]))
        print(f"  Similarity(pos_{i}, pos_{j}) = {sim:.4f}")

# Nearby positions are more similar than distant ones
print(f"\\n=== Distance Patterns ===")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_1)  = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[1]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[1])):.4f} (adjacent)")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_10) = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[10]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[10])):.4f} (distant)")
print(f"  sim(pos_0, pos_19) = {np.dot(pe[0], pe[19]) / (np.linalg.norm(pe[0]) * np.linalg.norm(pe[19])):.4f} (very distant)")

Vizualizarea modelelor de poziție

Codificarea sinusoidală creează un model de undă distinctiv. Dimensiunile inferioare oscilează lent (surprinzând informații poziționale largi), în timp ce dimensiunile superioare oscilează rapid (surprinzând poziția la nivel fin).

Python
import numpy as np

def sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model):
    pe = np.zeros((max_len, d_model))
    position = np.arange(max_len).reshape(-1, 1)
    div_term = np.exp(np.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model))
    pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(position * div_term)
    pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(position * div_term)
    return pe

max_len = 50
d_model = 32
pe = sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model)

# Visualize as a text-based heatmap
print("=== Positional Encoding Heatmap (first 20 positions, 16 dims) ===")
print("      " + "".join(f" d{i:<3}" for i in range(0, 16)))
print("      " + "-" * 64)

for pos in range(20):
    row = f"p{pos:<3} | "
    for dim in range(16):
        val = pe[pos, dim]
        if val > 0.5:
            row += "  ++ "
        elif val > 0.0:
            row += "  +  "
        elif val > -0.5:
            row += "  -  "
        else:
            row += "  -- "
    print(row)

print("\\nLegend: ++ (>0.5), + (0 to 0.5), - (-0.5 to 0), -- (<-0.5)")
print("\\nNotice: Low dimensions (d0,d1) change slowly across positions")
print("        High dimensions (d14,d15) oscillate more rapidly")

# Show the wave pattern for specific dimensions
print("\\n=== Dimension 0 (slow wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 0] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")

print("=== Dimension 6 (medium wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 6] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")

print("=== Dimension 14 (fast wave) ===")
wave = "".join("*" if pe[p, 14] > 0 else "." for p in range(50))
print(f"  {wave}")
print("(* = positive, . = negative)")

Abordarea 2: Embedding-uri poziționale învățate (GPT-2)

GPT-2 adoptă o abordare mai simplă: în loc să calculeze pozițiile cu formule, învață un embedding separat pentru fiecare poziție, la fel cum învață embedding-urile de token-uri. Acesta este pur și simplu un alt tabel de căutare de embedding, dar indexat după poziție în loc de ID-ul token-ului.

Proprietate Sinusoidală (Transformer original) Învățată (GPT-2)
Cum funcționează Formulă matematică fixă Învățată în timpul antrenamentului
Antrenabilă? Nu (fixă) Da (retropropagare)
Extrapolare Poate extinde dincolo de lungimea de antrenament Limitată la lungimea maximă de antrenament
Parametri Zero parametri suplimentari max_len × d_model parametri
Performanță Bună Ușor mai bună în practică
Utilizată de Transformer-ul original, unele modele GPT-2, GPT-3, BERT

import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    """Simple embedding layer."""
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

# === GPT-2 Style: Learned Positional Embeddings ===
np.random.seed(42)

vocab_size = 100
max_seq_len = 20
embed_dim = 8

# TWO separate embedding tables
token_embedding = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)  # shape: (100, 8)
position_embedding = Embedding(max_seq_len, embed_dim)  # shape: (20, 8)

print(f"Token embedding table:    ({vocab_size}, {embed_dim})")
print(f"Position embedding table: ({max_seq_len}, {embed_dim})")

# Simulate processing a sentence

seq_len = len(token_ids)

print(f"\\nToken embeddings shape: {tok_emb.shape}")

# Position embeddings: look up by position index [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
position_ids = list(range(seq_len))
pos_emb = position_embedding.forward(position_ids)
print(f"Position embeddings shape: {pos_emb.shape}")

# === THE KEY STEP: Add them together! ===
input_embeddings = tok_emb + pos_emb
print(f"Combined embeddings shape: {input_embeddings.shape}")

# Show the combination for one token
print(f"\\n=== Token at position 0 (token_id=42) ===")
print(f"  Token embedding:    {tok_emb[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position embedding: {pos_emb[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Combined (sum):     {input_embeddings[0].round(3)}")

# The same token at different positions gets different representations!
print(f"\\n=== Same token (id=42) at different positions ===")
same_tok = token_embedding.forward([42, 42, 42])
diff_pos = position_embedding.forward([0, 5, 15])
combined = same_tok + diff_pos
print(f"  Position  0: {combined[0].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position  5: {combined[1].round(3)}")
print(f"  Position 15: {combined[2].round(3)}")
print("  Same word, different representations due to position!")

# GPT-2 scale
print(f"\\n--- GPT-2 Scale ---")
print(f"Position embedding table: ({1024}, {768})")
print(f"Position parameters: {1024 * 768:,} = ~786K")
print(f"Max sequence length: 1024 tokens")
✅ De ce adunare, nu concatenare?

V-ați putea întreba: de ce adunăm embedding-urile de token și de poziție în loc să le concatenam? Adunarea păstrează dimensionalitatea aceeași (d_model), în timp ce concatenarea ar dubla-o la 2 * d_model. Cercetările arată că adunarea funcționează la fel de bine, iar modelul învață să folosească dimensiuni diferite pentru informațiile de token vs. poziție în timpul antrenamentului. Acest lucru păstrează și arhitectura mai simplă și mai eficientă din punct de vedere al memoriei.

Reprezentarea completă a intrării

Să vedem acum imaginea completă a modului în care GPT-2 își construiește intrarea:

Pipeline-ul de intrare GPT-2

Text brut: "The cat sat on the mat"

      └───────────────┘
              |
              v
Token IDs: [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]
              |                        |
              v                        v
   ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
   │ Embedding token  │    │ Embedding poziție │
   │ tabel (50257x768)│    │ tabel (1024x768) │
   └──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘
              |                        |
              v                        v
   tok_emb (6, 768)        pos_emb (6, 768)
              \                       /
               \                     /
                \      Adunare      /
                 \   element cu    /
                  v   element     v
            ┌──────────────────────┐
            │  input_emb (6, 768)  │
            │  = tok_emb + pos_emb │
            └──────────────────────┘
                      |
                      v
              Către straturile Transformer
Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale
    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

class GPT2InputEmbedding:
    """
    Complete GPT-2 input embedding: token + position.
    This is what the first layer of GPT-2 does.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, max_seq_len, embed_dim):
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len
        self.token_embedding = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.position_embedding = Embedding(max_seq_len, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, token_ids):
        seq_len = len(token_ids)
        if seq_len > self.max_seq_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds maximum {self.max_seq_len}"
            )

        # Token embeddings
        tok_emb = self.token_embedding.forward(token_ids)

        # Position embeddings (positions 0, 1, 2, ..., seq_len-1)
        pos_ids = list(range(seq_len))
        pos_emb = self.position_embedding.forward(pos_ids)

        # Combine by addition
        return tok_emb + pos_emb

# === Full pipeline demo ===
np.random.seed(42)

model_input = GPT2InputEmbedding(
    vocab_size=50257,   # GPT-2 vocabulary
    max_seq_len=1024,   # GPT-2 max context
    embed_dim=768       # GPT-2 embedding dimension
)

# Simulated token IDs (as if from a BPE tokenizer)
token_ids = [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]
words = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]

print("=== GPT-2 Input Embedding Pipeline ===")
print(f"Input tokens: {list(zip(words, token_ids))}")

input_emb = model_input.forward(token_ids)
print(f"Output shape: {input_emb.shape}")
print(f"  ({len(token_ids)} tokens, each with 768-dim embedding)")

# Show that "the" (pos 0) and "the" (pos 4) now differ
print(f"\\n'The' at position 0: [{input_emb[0][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"'the' at position 4: [{input_emb[4][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"Same word, different positions -> different representations!")

# Total parameters
tok_params = 50257 * 768
pos_params = 1024 * 768
print(f"\\n--- Parameter Count ---")
print(f"Token embedding:    {tok_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Position embedding: {pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Total input layer:  {tok_params + pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"That is {(tok_params + pos_params) / 1e6:.1f}M parameters just for the input!")

Lungimea maximă a secvenței și implicațiile sale

Cu embedding-uri poziționale învățate, modelul are o lungime maximă rigidă a secvenței. GPT-2 a fost antrenat cu max_seq_len = 1024, ceea ce înseamnă că poate procesa doar secvențe de până la 1024 de token-uri. Dacă încercați să-i furnizați mai multe, modelul pur și simplu nu are embedding-uri poziționale pentru pozițiile de dincolo de 1023.

Aceasta este una dintre limitările cheie pe care abordările mai noi încearcă să le rezolve:

📏 RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding)

Utilizat în LLaMA și multe modele moderne. Codifică poziția ca rotații în subspații 2D, permițând o extrapolare mai bună la secvențe mai lungi.

🔗 ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases)

Utilizat în BLOOM. Adaugă un bias liniar bazat pe distanța dintre token-uri direct în scorurile de atenție, fără a fi nevoie de embedding-uri poziționale.

📚 Legătura cu cartea

În „Build an LLM from Scratch”, Raschka implementează abordarea GPT-2 cu embedding-uri poziționale învățate. Parametrul cfg["context_length"] (1024 pentru GPT-2) determină dimensiunea tabelului de embedding pozițional. Acesta este definit chiar la începutul clasei modelului, alături de stratul de embedding al token-urilor.

Codificări poziționale relative vs. absolute

Tot ce am discutat până acum folosește poziții absolute: poziția 0, poziția 1 etc. O alternativă este codificarea pozițională relativă, care codifică distanța dintre token-uri în loc de pozițiile lor absolute.

Aspect Absolută (GPT-2) Relativă (T5 etc.)
Ce se codifică Indexul poziției (0, 1, 2, ...) Distanța dintre token-uri (i - j)
Unde se aplică Adăugat la embedding-urile de intrare Adăugat la scorurile de atenție
Generalizare la lungime Limitată la lungimea de antrenament Generalizare mai bună
Complexitate Tabel simplu de căutare Implementare mai complexă

Pentru implementarea noastră GPT-2, vom rămâne cu embedding-urile absolute învățate — sunt mai simple și funcționează bine în practică.

⚠️ Greșeală frecventă

O eroare comună la implementarea embedding-urilor poziționale este uitarea limitării lungimii secvenței. Dacă tabelul de embedding pozițional al modelului dvs. are 1024 de intrări și îi furnizați o secvență de 1025 de token-uri, veți obține o eroare de index în afara limitelor. Validați întotdeauna lungimea intrării față de max_seq_len înainte de procesare.

Rezumat

📌 Idei cheie

  • Transformer-ele procesează toate token-urile în paralel și nu au un simț inerent al ordinii
  • Embedding-urile poziționale codifică locul fiecărui token în secvență
  • GPT-2 folosește embedding-uri poziționale învățate (un al doilea tabel de căutare)
  • Embedding-urile de token + poziție sunt adunate element cu element pentru a forma intrarea
  • Lungimea maximă a secvenței este fixată de dimensiunea tabelului de embedding pozițional

👉 Ce urmează

Acum avem reprezentarea completă a intrării pentru LLM-ul nostru. În Lecția 12, vom construi pipeline-ul complet de preprocesare a datelor care preia text brut și produce loturi de secvențe de token-uri încorporate, gata de antrenament.

🧠 Quick Check

Q1: Why do Transformers need positional embeddings but RNNs do not?

A: RNNs process tokens one at a time in sequence, so position is implicit in the processing order. Transformers process all tokens in parallel, so position must be explicitly encoded.

Q2: What is the shape of GPT-2's position embedding table?

A: (1024, 768) — 1024 positions (max sequence length) times 768 embedding dimensions, totaling ~786K parameters.

Q3: Why add token and position embeddings instead of concatenating them?

A: Addition preserves the embedding dimension (d_model), keeping the architecture simpler and more memory-efficient. The model learns to partition dimensions for token vs. position information during training.

⏱ 45 λεπτα αναγνωση 💻 Πρακτικη εξασκηση 🎯 Μεσαιο

Γιατι Εχει Σημασια η Θεση;

Σκεφτειτε αυτες τις δυο προτασεις:

  • "Dog bites man" — ενα κοινοτυπο γεγονος
  • "Man bites dog" — ειδηση πρωτοσελιδα!

Ιδιες λεξεις, εντελως διαφορετικες σημασιες. Η σειρα των λεξεων ειναι ουσιαστικη για την κατανοηση της γλωσσας. Αλλα εδω ειναι το προβλημα: τα token embeddings απο τη Διαλεξη 10 αναθετουν ακριβως το ιδιο διανυσμα στο "dog" ανεξαρτητα αν εμφανιζεται πρωτο η τελευταιο στην προταση. Το στρωμα embedding δεν εχει καμια εννοια θεσης.

Αυτο διαφερει θεμελιωδως απο τα αναδρομικα νευρωνικα δικτυα (RNNs), που επεξεργαζονται tokens ενα καθε φορα με τη σειρα. Οι Transformers, αντιθετα, επεξεργαζονται ολα τα tokens ταυτοχρονα παραλληλα. Αυτος ο παραλληλισμος ειναι που τα κανει γρηγορα, αλλα σημαινει οτι δεν εχουν εγγενη εννοια σειρας ακολουθιας. Πρεπει να εισαγαγουμε ρητα την πληροφορια θεσης.

💡 Αναλογια: Αριθμοι Θεσεων στο Θεατρο

Σκεφτειτε τα tokens ως θεατες και την ακολουθια ως θεατρο. Η λεξη "love" σημαινει το ιδιο πραγμα ανεξαρτητα απο το ποιος τη λεει (token embedding), αλλα το μοντελο πρεπει να ξερει οτι καθεται στη θεση 3, οχι στη θεση 7 — επειδη το που καθεται αλλαζει τη σημασια της προτασης. Τα positional embeddings ειναι σαν ετικετες αριθμου θεσης που φοραει καθε token.

Το Προβλημα: Οι Transformers Ειναι Τυφλοι στη Θεση

Για να το κανουμε συγκεκριμενο, σκεφτειτε πως ενας Transformer επεξεργαζεται μια ακολουθια. Μετα το στρωμα token embedding, εχουμε εναν πινακα σχηματος (sequence_length, embed_dim). Χωρις πληροφορια θεσης, το μοντελο το βλεπει αυτο ως συνολο (μη διατεταγμενη συλλογη), οχι ως ακολουθια (διατεταγμενη λιστα).

Το Προβλημα Θεσης

"The cat sat"                    "sat cat The"

Token embeddings:                Token embeddings:
┌──────────┐                     ┌──────────┐
│ emb("The") │                     │ emb("sat") │
│ emb("cat") │   No position      │ emb("cat") │   No position
│ emb("sat") │  ============>     │ emb("The") │  ============>
└──────────┘    Same bag of       └──────────┘    Same bag of

  Without position info, these are IDENTICAL to the model.

Χρειαζομαστε εναν τροπο να κανουμε καθε θεση μοναδικη. Οι δυο κυριες προσεγγισεις ειναι η ημιτονοειδης κωδικοποιηση και τα εκπαιδευμενα embeddings.

Προσεγγιση 1: Ημιτονοειδης Positional Encoding

Το αρχικο αρθρο "Attention Is All You Need" (Vaswani et al., 2017) προτεινε τη χρηση συναρτησεων ημιτονου και συνημιτονου διαφορετικων συχνοτητων για την κωδικοποιηση θεσης. Ο τυπος ειναι:

# For even dimensions (2i):
PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

# For odd dimensions (2i+1):
PE(pos, 2i+1) = cos(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))

Αυτο δημιουργει ενα μοναδικο μοτιβο για καθε θεση. Οι βασικες ιδιοτητες:

🔍 Μοναδικα Μοτιβα

Καθε θεση παιρνει ξεχωριστο διανυσμα. Καμια δυο θεσεις δεν μοιραζονται την ιδια κωδικοποιηση.

📏 Φραγμενες Τιμες

Το ημιτονο και το συνημιτονο ειναι παντα μεταξυ -1 και +1, διατηρωντας τις τιμες αριθμητικα σταθερες.

♻️ Σχετικες Θεσεις

Το μοντελο μπορει να μαθει να εστιαζει σε σχετικες θεσεις επειδη το PE(pos+k) μπορει να εκφραστει ως γραμμικη συναρτηση του PE(pos).

🔄 Γενικευση

Μπορει να επεκταθει σε μηκη ακολουθιας που δεν ειδωθηκαν κατα την εκπαιδευση (θεωρητικα).

import numpy as np

def sinusoidal_position_encoding(max_len, d_model):
    """
    Create sinusoidal positional encodings.

    Args:
        max_len: Maximum sequence length
        d_model: Embedding dimension (must be even)
    Returns:
        numpy array of shape (max_len, d_model)
    """
    pe = np.zeros((max_len, d_model))
    position = np.arange(max_len).reshape(-1, 1)  # (max_len, 1)

    # Compute the division term: 10000^(2i/d_model)
    div_term = np.exp(
        np.arange(0, d_model, 2) * -(np.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )

    # Apply sin to even indices, cos to odd indices
    pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(position * div_term)  # even dims
    pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(position * div_term)  # odd dims

    return pe

# Generate encodings

import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    """Simple embedding layer."""
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale

    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

# === GPT-2 Style: Learned Positional Embeddings ===
np.random.seed(42)

max_seq_len = 20

# Simulate processing a sentence

Μπορει να αναρωτιεστε: γιατι προσθετουμε τα embeddings token και θεσης αντι να τα συνενωνουμε; Η προσθεση διατηρει τη διαστατικοτητα ιδια (d_model), ενω η συνενωση θα την διπλασιαζε σε 2 * d_model. Η ερευνα δειχνει οτι η προσθεση λειτουργει εξισου καλα, και το μοντελο μαθαινει να χρησιμοποιει διαφορετικες διαστασεις για πληροφορια token εναντιον θεσης κατα την εκπαιδευση. Αυτο διατηρει επισης την αρχιτεκτονικη απλουστερη και πιο αποδοτικη σε μνημη.

Python
import numpy as np

class Embedding:
    def __init__(self, num_embeddings, embedding_dim):
        scale = np.sqrt(1.0 / embedding_dim)
        self.weight = np.random.randn(num_embeddings, embedding_dim) * scale
    def forward(self, ids):
        return self.weight[np.array(ids)]

class GPT2InputEmbedding:
    """
    Complete GPT-2 input embedding: token + position.
    This is what the first layer of GPT-2 does.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, max_seq_len, embed_dim):
        self.max_seq_len = max_seq_len
        self.token_embedding = Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.position_embedding = Embedding(max_seq_len, embed_dim)

    def forward(self, token_ids):
        seq_len = len(token_ids)
        if seq_len > self.max_seq_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds maximum {self.max_seq_len}"
            )

        # Token embeddings
        tok_emb = self.token_embedding.forward(token_ids)

        # Position embeddings (positions 0, 1, 2, ..., seq_len-1)
        pos_ids = list(range(seq_len))
        pos_emb = self.position_embedding.forward(pos_ids)

        # Combine by addition
        return tok_emb + pos_emb

# === Full pipeline demo ===
np.random.seed(42)

model_input = GPT2InputEmbedding(
    vocab_size=50257,   # GPT-2 vocabulary
    max_seq_len=1024,   # GPT-2 max context
    embed_dim=768       # GPT-2 embedding dimension
)

# Simulated token IDs (as if from a BPE tokenizer)
token_ids = [464, 3797, 3332, 319, 262, 2603]
words = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]

print("=== GPT-2 Input Embedding Pipeline ===")
print(f"Input tokens: {list(zip(words, token_ids))}")

input_emb = model_input.forward(token_ids)
print(f"Output shape: {input_emb.shape}")
print(f"  ({len(token_ids)} tokens, each with 768-dim embedding)")

# Show that "the" (pos 0) and "the" (pos 4) now differ
print(f"\\n'The' at position 0: [{input_emb[0][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"'the' at position 4: [{input_emb[4][:4].round(4)}...]")
print(f"Same word, different positions -> different representations!")

# Total parameters
tok_params = 50257 * 768
pos_params = 1024 * 768
print(f"\\n--- Parameter Count ---")
print(f"Token embedding:    {tok_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Position embedding: {pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"Total input layer:  {tok_params + pos_params:>12,} params")
print(f"That is {(tok_params + pos_params) / 1e6:.1f}M parameters just for the input!")

Μεγιστο Μηκος Ακολουθιας και οι Επιπτωσεις του

Με εκπαιδευμενα positional embeddings, το μοντελο εχει αυστηρο μεγιστο μηκος ακολουθιας. Το GPT-2 εκπαιδευτηκε με max_seq_len = 1024, που σημαινει οτι μπορει να επεξεργαστει ακολουθιες μεχρι 1024 tokens. Αν προσπαθησετε να του δωσετε περισσοτερα, το μοντελο απλα δεν εχει positional embeddings για θεσεις περαν της 1023.

Αυτος ειναι ενας απο τους βασικους περιορισμους που νεωτερες προσεγγισεις προσπαθουν να αντιμετωπισουν:

📏 RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding)

Χρησιμοποιειται στο LLaMA και πολλα συγχρονα μοντελα. Κωδικοποιει τη θεση ως περιστροφες σε 2D υποχωρους, επιτρεποντας καλυτερη επεκτασιμοτητα σε μεγαλυτερες ακολουθιες.

🔗 ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases)

Χρησιμοποιειται στο BLOOM. Προσθετει γραμμικη πολωση βασισμενη στην αποσταση tokens απευθειας στα σκορ προσοχης, χωρις να χρειαζονται positional embeddings.

📚 Συνδεση με το Βιβλιο

Στο "Build an LLM from Scratch", ο Raschka υλοποιει την προσεγγιση του GPT-2 με εκπαιδευμενα positional embeddings. Η παραμετρος cfg["context_length"] (1024 για το GPT-2) καθοριζει το μεγεθος του πινακα positional embedding. Αυτο οριζεται αμεσως στην αρχη της κλασης του μοντελου, μαζι με το στρωμα token embedding.

Σχετικα εναντιον Απολυτα Positional Encodings

Ολα οσα εχουμε συζητησει μεχρι τωρα χρησιμοποιουν απολυτες θεσεις: θεση 0, θεση 1 κτλ. Μια εναλλακτικη ειναι το σχετικο positional encoding, που κωδικοποιει την αποσταση μεταξυ tokens αντι για τις απολυτες θεσεις τους.

Πτυχη Απολυτο (GPT-2) Σχετικο (T5 κ.α.)
Τι κωδικοποιειται Δεικτης θεσης (0, 1, 2, ...) Αποσταση μεταξυ tokens (i - j)
Που εφαρμοζεται Προστιθεται στα embeddings εισοδου Προστιθεται στα σκορ προσοχης
Γενικευση μηκους Περιορισμενο στο μηκος εκπαιδευσης Καλυτερη γενικευση
Πολυπλοκοτητα Απλος πινακας αναζητησης Πιο πολυπλοκη υλοποιηση

Για την υλοποιηση GPT-2 μας, θα παραμεινουμε με απολυτα εκπαιδευμενα embeddings — ειναι απλουστερα και λειτουργουν καλα στην πραξη.

⚠️ Συνηθισμενο Λαθος

Ενα συνηθισμενο σφαλμα κατα την υλοποιηση positional embeddings ειναι να ξεχνατε να περιορισετε το μηκος ακολουθιας. Αν ο πινακας positional embedding του μοντελου σας εχει 1024 εγγραφες και του δωσετε ακολουθια 1025 tokens, θα παρετε σφαλμα index-out-of-bounds. Επαληθευετε παντα το μηκος εισοδου σε σχεση με το max_seq_len πριν την επεξεργασια.

Περιληψη

📌 Βασικα Συμπερασματα

  • Οι Transformers επεξεργαζονται ολα τα tokens παραλληλα και δεν εχουν εγγενη αισθηση σειρας
  • Τα positional embeddings κωδικοποιουν που βρισκεται καθε token στην ακολουθια
  • Το GPT-2 χρησιμοποιει εκπαιδευμενα positional embeddings (δευτερος πινακας αναζητησης)
  • Τα embeddings token και θεσης προστιθενται στοιχειο προς στοιχειο για να σχηματισουν την εισοδο
  • Το μεγιστο μηκος ακολουθιας καθοριζεται απο το μεγεθος του πινακα positional embedding

🧠 Quick Check

Q1: Why do Transformers need positional embeddings but RNNs do not?

A: RNNs process tokens one at a time in sequence, so position is implicit in the processing order. Transformers process all tokens in parallel, so position must be explicitly encoded.

Q2: What is the shape of GPT-2's position embedding table?

A: (1024, 768) — 1024 positions (max sequence length) times 768 embedding dimensions, totaling ~786K parameters.

Q3: Why add token and position embeddings instead of concatenating them?

A: Addition preserves the embedding dimension (d_model), keeping the architecture simpler and more memory-efficient. The model learns to partition dimensions for token vs. position information during training.
